newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso closes soft on pre-Thanksgiving swaps.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso closes soft on pre-Thanksgiving swaps.

text.p: The Mexican peso closed weaker on Wednesday due to swaps ahead of the U.S. Thanksgiving holiday, traders said.

"The market was very calm indeed...I feel most dealers had covered positions and that some were even long on dollars," said a trader. The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate closed 1.7 and 1.2 centavos, respectively, at 7.8890/7.8930 and 7.8730/7.8770 per dollar.
The same-day peso closed earlier 0.1 of a centavo firmer at 7.8580/7.8610 per dollar.

Traders said dealers sold dollars in the same-day market to buy them back at 48-hours. The advantage was that, with U.S. markets closed for Thanksgiving on Thursday, 48-hour contracts did not need to be paid for until Monday, with pesos that could meanwhile be invested in the Mexican money market.
Traders said falls in primary interest rates on Tuesday night had little effect on the peso. "Rates on Cetes were still good even if they did fall a little," said a dealer.
Traders said they expected the Mexican foreign exchange market to be very quiet on Thursday due to U.S. financial markets being closed. There will thus be no same-day peso trading on Thursday.
